title: Tanzanian Tomato Sauce
community: The universal base sauce of Tanzanian cooking
author: Mama Salima
desc: Tanzanian Mchuzi wa Nyanya — the foundational tomato and onion sauce that underpins virtually every Tanzanian stew, curry, and vegetable dish. Learning to make this well is learning the foundation of Tanzanian cooking.
longDesc: The tomato-onion sauce is the building block of Tanzanian cooking — every stew, every curry, every vegetable dish begins with this foundation. The difference between a great Tanzanian cook and an average one is the quality of this base: properly golden onions, completely reduced tomatoes, well-bloomed spices.
ingredients: 6 large ripe tomatoes — diced (or 400g tinned tomatoes)
steps: Cook onions until deeply golden — 10—12 minutes. Do not rush.
Add garlic and ginger. Cook 1 minute.
Add tomato paste. Stir and cook 2 minutes.
Add fresh or tinned tomatoes and all spices.
Cook uncovered, stirring regularly, for 12—15 minutes until sauce is thick, dark, and oil has separated from the tomatoes.
This is the finished base — add other ingredients to it.
chefTips: Golden onions are the foundation — do not rush them.
The oil separating from the tomatoes signals the sauce is properly reduced.
This sauce can be made in large batches and frozen for up to 3 months.
commonMistakes: Pale, under-cooked onions — bitter, raw flavour.
cookingScience: The oil separating from the tomatoes during reduction signals that most of the water has evaporated and the tomato sugars have concentrated. This is the Maillard and caramelisation point — where maximum flavour development has occurred.
sustainabilityTips: Make in large batches and freeze — reduces fuel use and always available.
servedWith: Add protein or vegetables to build any Tanzanian stew
healthBenefits: Very low calorie as a base.
culturalNote: Mchuzi wa nyanya is Tanzanian cooking's most important skill — the foundation that every Tanzanian cook learns before anything else. The quality of this base determines the quality of every dish built upon it.
